title: [Installer] Per-user upgrades plan related bundles twice and leave broken uninstall entries
author: LegendaryBlair

linked_work.relevance: External engine bug matching the duplicate related-bundle detection and plan sequence described in the PowerToys report.

judgment.rationale: The reporter provided deterministic Burn logs, the exact external WiX engine issue, and a PowerToys-specific mitigation seam in SilentFilesInUseBAFunctions. That is already enough to approve a bounded design without asking the reporter for generic diagnostics.
evidence: The issue body shows the same per-user bundle detected twice, then planned twice, then the second uninstall fails with 0x80070003 after the first removed the cached executable.
The report ties the behavior to wixtoolset/issues#7675, where HKCU per-user related bundles are surfaced twice because Burn scans both 32-bit and 64-bit registry views.
Directory.Packages.props and installer/PowerToysSetupVNext/PowerToysBootstrapperVNext.wixproj confirm that PowerToys currently builds the bootstrapper with WiX 5.0.2.
installer/PowerToysSetupVNext/SilentFilesInUseBA/SilentFilesInUseBAFunctions.cpp already overrides OnPlanBegin, giving PowerToys a product-side BAFunctions seam for per-plan deduplication.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a bounded BAFunctions mitigation that suppresses duplicate per-user related-bundle plan entries while preserving the first occurrence and rollback behavior.

fix_assessment.rationale: A repository-local mitigation is applicable in the PowerToys BAFunctions layer even while the upstream WiX engine defect remains open.

proposed_fixes.title: Deduplicate repeated per-user related-bundle plan entries in SilentFilesInUseBAFunctions
proposed_fixes.root_cause: WiX 5.0.2 can surface the same HKCU per-user related bundle twice during planning, so PowerToys needs to suppress only the second occurrence before Burn tries to uninstall the same cached bundle twice.
plan: Add a per-plan case-insensitive set of related bundle IDs to CSilentFilesInUseBAFunctions.
Clear the set in OnPlanBegin and override OnPlanRelatedBundle to preserve the first requested state while forcing BOOTSTRAPPER_REQUEST_STATE_NONE for later duplicate occurrences.
Log duplicate suppression and validate per-user upgrade plus rollback behavior without changing ARP or dependency cleanup ownership.
verification: In a per-user upgrade, exactly one uninstall should be requested and executed for the old bundle.
The upgrade should no longer emit the second 0x80070003 CreateProcessW failure or leave a stale Installed Apps entry pointing to a removed cached EXE.
Per-machine upgrade behavior and rollback should remain unchanged.

confidence.rationale: The logs, external engine bug, and available PowerToys BAFunctions seam line up cleanly, leaving only implementation validation around callback ordering and rollback.

issue_context.summary: Per-user PowerToys upgrades can plan the same related bundle twice, causing the second uninstall to fail after the first already removed the cached bundle executable.
known_information: The issue body includes deterministic Burn detection, planning, uninstall, cache-removal, and failure log snippets.
The report identifies the matching external WiX engine issue and documents why HKCU per-user bundles are affected.
PowerToys uses WiX 5.0.2 and ships a BAFunctions DLL that already participates in planning callbacks.
inferences: Suppressing the second related-bundle plan entry in BAFunctions is lower risk than ad-hoc registry cleanup after the installer succeeds.
The highest remaining risk is not root-cause uncertainty but ensuring the product-side mitigation does not disturb rollback or legitimate first-occurrence handling.
issue_context.analysis: A fresh reporter ZIP would not change the design decision because the retained Burn logs already identify the engine behavior and the precise mitigation seam.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue body, the maintainer follow-up, labels, and timeline state.
Confirmed the WiX 5.0.2 package references in Directory.Packages.props and PowerToysBootstrapperVNext.wixproj.
Inspected installer/PowerToysSetupVNext/SilentFilesInUseBA/SilentFilesInUseBAFunctions.cpp and confirmed it currently has no OnPlanRelatedBundle deduplication.
Checked for a linked PowerToys fix PR and found none.

actions.label: Approve per-user bundle dedupe fix design
actions.note: Keep the work bounded to BAFunctions related-bundle planning while the upstream WiX engine issue remains open.
